deities: Goddess Sati as Alopi Devi (formless - worshipped as a wooden doli/palanquin, no idol)

history.period: Antiquity uncertain - some historians suggest ~11th century (verify); Nagara-style shrine
history.summary: Alopi Devi Mandir in Alopibagh, near the Sangam, is one of India's most unusual Shakti Peethas: there is no idol at all, and a wooden doli (palanquin) on a marble platform over a small kund is worshipped as the goddess, symbolising her 'disappearance' (Alopi). Tradition holds this is where the last part of Sati's body fell and vanished; one popular account says two fingers of Sati fell here (verify), though the Wikipedia article notes the rival claim that Prayagraj's Shakti peeth is the Lalita Devi temple (verify). Maratha warrior Shreenath Mahadji Shinde developed the Sangam area during his 1771-1772 stay, and Maharani Baizabai Scindia renovated Sangam ghats and temples in the 1800s. A Shankaracharya ashram of Jyotishpeeth stands opposite. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Allahabad' - the city was officially renamed Prayagraj in 2018; documented as Prayagraj, locality Alopibagh.

name: Alopi Devi Mandir
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is the sacred city at the Triveni Sangam - the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati - and the site of the Kumbh and Magh Melas. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre as well as a historic city with the Mughal-era Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and Prayagraj University.

travel.road: Alopibagh area near Triveni Sangam; taxi, auto-rickshaw and local buses available

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (very crowded); morning and evening aartis
visitor_information.opening_hours: ~5:00 AM-9:00 PM daily (one source says 9:30 PM; verify). Free entry; photography restricted in sanctum
